questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943521/assets/2b8bbc9ae6b8bf8c441c8e2b534fb159f8180833e1891baa094f988d6a362117.png)

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(Bx)+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $D-B?$
questions.worked_solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T=\frac{3\pi }{4}-(-\frac{3\pi }{4})=\frac{6\pi }{4}=\frac{3\pi }{2}.
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\operatorname{tan}⁡(Bx+C)+D$ is given by 

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
\frac{3\pi }{2}=\frac{\pi }{B}\,⟹\,B=\frac{\pi }{(\frac{3\pi }{2})}=\frac{2}{3}.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the tangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $1$ units up. Hence, $D=1.$

Therefore, $D-B=1-(\frac{2}{3})=\frac{1}{3}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{2x}{3})+1.
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943521/assets/89efc20f1c6527d1bcd501f97ce585fb5a60e9791804f56d61f33653cf1a70d7.png)

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x+C),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
questions.worked_solution:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x+C) \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(3(x+\frac{C}{3}))\end{aligned}
$$

The factor $x+\frac{C}{3}$ indicates that the graph of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(3(x+\frac{C}{3}))$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943521/assets/f8617da98ea9d9fb48b8fef588b624c6961a299233836fe433c1819b697ca0fb.png)

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x)$ by $0-(-\frac{\pi }{12})=\frac{\pi }{12}$ units to the left. Therefore:

$$
\frac{C}{3}=\frac{\pi }{12}\,⟹\,C=\frac{\pi }{4}
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $\frac{\pi }{4}$ is in this interval, the value of $C$ is $\frac{\pi }{4}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943521/assets/015ca9336646a7545de842414ace2c2a695688e30653b2ed019000d69609d56d.png)

\frac{3C}{2}=\frac{\pi }{4}\,⟹\,C=(\frac{\pi }{4})(\frac{2}{3})\,⟹\,C=\frac{\pi }{6}
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $\frac{\pi }{6}$ is in this interval, the value of $C$ is $\frac{\pi }{6}.$

The graph above shows the function $y = \tan(Bx) + D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B + D?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T =  \dfrac{\pi}{5} - \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{5}\right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{5}.
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y = A\tan(Bx + C) + D$ is given by 

$$
T = \dfrac{\pi}{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
\dfrac{2\pi}{5} = \dfrac{\pi}{B} \quad\Longrightarrow \quad B = \dfrac{\pi}{\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)} = \dfrac{5}{2}.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the tangent function. The graph shows that the function has been translated by $1$ unit up. Hence, $D = 1.$

Therefore, 

$$
B + D =\dfrac{5}{2} +1 = \dfrac{7}{2}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y = \tan\left(\frac{5x}{2} \right) +1.
$$
